newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clal drops bid for Yotvata stake.
newsitem.headline: Clal drops bid for Yotvata stake.

text.p: Clal Industries Ltd has decided to end negotiations to buy half of an Israeli kibbutz-owned dairy called Yotvata, a company spokesman said on Sunday.
Clal made an offer last February to acquire 50 percent of Yotvata for 100 million shekels.

But the negotiations ran into problems when Yotvata brought in the Tnuva cooperative, the country's biggest food concern and the largest producer of milk and dairy products. Tnuva distributes Yotvata's products in most of Israel.

"They were proposing that Tnuva and Yotvata would have 74 percent and we would have 26 percent," the spokesman said. He said this did not fit in with Clal's strategy as the company wanted to be a dominant partner.
"We wanted to be a strategic, not a financial partner. We wanted to turn Yotvata into a major player in the dairy market."

Clal, one of Israel's largest holding concerns, is a subsidiary of Clal Israel. Its other interests in the food industry include a small manufacturer of frozen foods called Sunfrost Ltd and Jaf-Ora, a beverage maker.
